title: Open Sea, Free Flow, Włochy - 1036 waves at open sea
author: Piotrek Zyla
notes: Binaural (DPA 4560, Zoom F3, 96 kHz FLAC), recordist sitting on the stern of a sailing catamaran on the open sea near Sicily, evening. Continuous soft sloshing, gurgling and occasional gentle slaps of water on the hull; no shore, no breakers. Tonal scan finds no engine/hum lines (max prominence <5 dB); no voices or gulls seen. Wide stereo (LR corr 0.17), LRA 6.9, peak -2 dBFS. Spectrum has a natur

title: 六塊厝漁港, New Taipei City, Taiwan - Waves lapping the pier
author: Wu, Tsan-Cheng
notes: Rhythmic small waves lapping against a small concrete/wooden fishing pier (Zoom H2n MS+XY). Very regular lap every ~4-6 s, steady level (-26..-33 dB windows). STOP at 118 s: a boat engine arrives after ~125 s. Lossy source (ogg ~88 kbps, 16 kHz ceiling), so medium.

title: WWS Smallwaves
author: Work With Sounds / Torsten Nilsson
notes: Close, intimate small waves plopping and slapping against the hull of a small fishing boat in Gislövsläge harbour (Sweden). Clean, no tones or voices; quiet source (-38 LUFS, needs gain). Only ~63 s long, just above the 60 s minimum. Lossy ogg (106 kbps) but content is below 8 kHz anyway.

title: 長濱漁港, Changbin Township - In the fishing pier
author: Wu, Tsan-Cheng
notes: 'In the fishing pier, very large storm day' (Taiwan east coast; Zoom H2n MS+XY): big surges sloshing and slapping inside a fishing harbour/pier every 8-15 s, with spray hiss between; no wind rumble on the mic (<60 Hz only 5%), no voices or engines seen. Heard from the pier, not a beach. Lossy ogg (92 kbps, 16 kHz ceiling); level swings ~14 dB between surges (LRA 10.6), which suits a storm.

title: Estagnol de Gaudet, Orlu, Ariège, France - france_pyrenees_morning_rain on tent_thunder
author: clement.grumberg
notes: Steady rain drumming on a tent from inside (Pyrenees, FLAC 48 kHz). Dense, warm drumming (82% energy 250 Hz-2 kHz), LRA 4.3, no hum. Chosen window avoids handling/thunder thumps at ~12 s, ~107 s, ~150 s and ~210 s. A handful of single close drops hit 0 dBFS (clips at 30.2, 30.8, 35.5, 46.0, 53.1, 55.6 s, each only a few samples) - harmless after gain-down but noted. Nylon tent, not thatch.

title: The rain knocks on the roof of the tent, White Sea, Russia
author: Nikolaj Terent'ev
notes: Binaural (Zoom H4n + Roland CS-10EM) rain knocking on the roof of a tent, White Sea coast. Very steady, even texture 250 Hz-8 kHz, no low rumble, no voices; the steadiest stretch is 0-112 s (level drops ~4 dB after 115 s). Lighter and brighter than thatch-1 (patter rather than drumming). Lossy ogg 125 kbps.

title: Tromsø / Romsa Harbour, North Norway / Sápmi - Pontoon Creaking
author: anguscarlyle
notes: Floating pontoon squeezed against the stone quay, Tromsø harbour: soft wood/rubber creak, harmonic squeal from ~2 kHz upward with natural decay. Background has continuous wind/handling rumble below ~300 Hz, so hp 400 is needed; above 400 Hz the creak is +24 dB over the in-band floor. Single short creak.

title: Tromsø / Romsa Harbour, North Norway / Sápmi - Pontoon Creaking
author: anguscarlyle
notes: Floating pontoon squeezed against the stone quay, Tromsø harbour: soft wood/rubber creak, harmonic squeal from ~2 kHz upward with natural decay. Background has continuous wind/handling rumble below ~300 Hz, so hp 400 is needed; above 400 Hz the creak is +30 dB over the in-band floor. Two-part creak (push and release) with a short gap.

author: anguscarlyle
notes: Floating pontoon squeezed against the stone quay, Tromsø harbour: soft wood/rubber creak, harmonic squeal from ~2 kHz upward with natural decay. Background has continuous wind/handling rumble below ~300 Hz, so hp 400 is needed; above 400 Hz the creak is +37 dB over the in-band floor. Single long, strong creak.

Background has continuous wind/handling rumble below ~300 Hz, so hp 400 is needed; above 400 Hz the creak is +34 dB over the in-band floor. Creak sequence (three groans) as the pontoon rocks.

title: WP9R+W4 Ajaccio, France - the mooring rope.
author: kaoss012
notes: Mooring rope groaning/creaking under strain as a moored boat surges (Ajaccio harbour, Zoom H6): stick-slip creak at 263.5-265.5 s and 266-268.5 s, with water slosh and soft hull thumps under it. Isolation is poor (~15-20 dB in the 1.5-8 kHz band) and the thumps need hp ~150; use as an optional 'rope under strain' variation only.

title: XC1033904 Laughing Gull
author: David Darrell-Lambert
notes: One complete laughing-gull long call: soft rising lead-in notes then the full 'ha-ha-ha-haah-haah' series (fundamental ~850 Hz, harmonics to ~8 kHz), natural tail kept; clean gaps before and after. Background is soft surf wash below ~700 Hz, which the hp removes. Lossless 24-bit/48 kHz WAV source (stereo, use as mono). In-band SNR ~38 dB; lowest note ~800 Hz. Recorded Treasure Island, Pinellas Cou

title: XC447329 Laughing Gull
author: David Darrell-Lambert
notes: Second half of a long call: rhythmic run of 'ha' notes slowing into long 'haah' notes (fundamental ~900 Hz, rich harmonics), ends cleanly with a natural tail. A second bird's thin tonal call earlier in the file (2.2-5.4 s) is outside the cut. Close and loud; surf wash below ~700 Hz removed by the hp. In-band SNR ~37 dB. Recorded Treasure Island, Pinellas County, Florida, 2016-08-27 (XC type: call,

title: XC169206 Laughing Gull
author: Paul Marvin
notes: A single short 'kow' call (~0.5 s, fundamental ~1.1 kHz with harmonics to 6 kHz) with clean silence either side - a short variant for sparse placement. A faint steady noise band ~0.7-1.1 kHz (distant surf/marsh) sits ~30 dB below. In-band SNR ~34 dB. Recorded Shiloh Marsh, Merritt Island National Wildlife Refuge, Volusia County, Florida, 2014-02-25 (XC type: call, rated A).

title: XC169206 Laughing Gull
author: Paul Marvin
notes: Full long call from a different bird and site: fast run of short notes building into long laughing notes and ending with two separated 'kah' notes, natural tail kept. Same faint ~0.7-1.1 kHz background band ~30 dB down. In-band SNR ~35 dB. Recorded Shiloh Marsh, Merritt Island National Wildlife Refuge, Volusia County, Florida, 2014-02-25 (XC type: call, rated A).

title: XC145812 Laughing Gull
author: Paul Marvin
notes: One harsher, scratchier call (~0.5 s, energy 1-5 kHz) - a different call type for variety; clean background before and after (in-band SNR ~41 dB). Medium confidence only because this rasping call is less typical than the laughing series (identified as laughing gull by the recordist). Recorded Biolab Road, Canaveral National Seashore, Brevard County, Florida, 2013-08-15 (XC type: call, rated A).

title: XC1034355 Royal Tern
author: David Darrell-Lambert
notes: One royal tern 'keer-reet' call (~0.35 s, pulsed, fundamental ~2 kHz, harmonics to 9 kHz). Faint shorebird peeps (~3.5-4.5 kHz) just before/after sit ~25 dB down. Lossless 24-bit/48 kHz source. In-band SNR ~39 dB. Recorded Treasure Island, Pinellas County, Florida, 2016-08-28 (XC type: call, rated A).

title: XC1034355 Royal Tern
author: David Darrell-Lambert
notes: Another royal tern call from the same session, louder and a little longer (~0.5 s, pulsed with a falling end), natural tail, clean gaps. In-band SNR ~45 dB. Recorded Treasure Island, Pinellas County, Florida, 2016-08-28 (XC type: call, rated A).

title: XC560599 Royal Tern
author: Russ Wigh
notes: Single royal tern call (~0.35 s, harsh pulsed 'keer', ~1-5 kHz) from a different bird and site; faint small-bird chips and a steady ~7 kHz insect line in the background ~25 dB down; surf rumble below 400 Hz removed by the hp. In-band SNR ~36 dB. Recorded Skidaway Island, Chatham County, GA USA, 2019-08-16 (XC type: call, rated A).

title: XC383121 Cabot's Tern
author: David Darrell-Lambert
notes: Cabot's (sandwich) tern 'kirr-ick' call (~0.3 s, 1.2-6 kHz) - the sandwich-tern option of this pool. Strong surf/wind wash at 200-700 Hz in the source sits under the call: the hp at 1 kHz is required. In-band SNR ~36 dB above 1 kHz. Recorded Treasure Island, Pinellas County, Florida, 2016-08-27 (XC type: call, rated A).

title: XC383121 Cabot's Tern
author: David Darrell-Lambert
notes: A second Cabot's (sandwich) tern call from the same bird, slightly different contour; same surf wash below ~700 Hz, hp 1 kHz required. In-band SNR ~36 dB above 1 kHz. Recorded Treasure Island, Pinellas County, Florida, 2016-08-27 (XC type: call, rated A).

notes: Guiana dolphins (Sotalia guianensis, a small coastal dolphin closely related to bottlenose) underwater, Brazil (Baía dos Golfinhos), 2004-05-25: a dense burst of rising whistles (6-18 kHz) and click trains with snapping-shrimp crackle. author: Luciara Azevedo (iNaturalist: luciaraazevedo)
notes: Later stretch of the same Guiana-dolphin recording: whistles (incl. a looped contour at ~10 kHz), click trains and buzzes; quieter middle (15-17 s) gives it a natural ebb. Same caveats: hp required for the low rumble; whistles 6-18 kHz.
